text.p: World number one Greg Norman examined Ballesteros's scores closely, shook his head sadly and then declared: "We bleed for Seve.
"This has got to be killing him."
Despite having a lesson from Norman on the practice range on Tuesday, Ballesteros had just compiled a 12-over-par 84 in the second round of the Dubai Desert Classic and missed the cut by 13 shots.
It was the former world number one's worst score in the three tournaments he has played this year and the third cut he had missed.
"We bleed for Ian Baker-Finch and we bleed for Seve," said Norman, referring first to the Australian former British Open champion who has made only one cut in two-and-a-half years.
"We all hate to see that. Both have been great players and great guys, our hearts go out to them.
"I know I wouldn't want to be in their position, it's got to be a horrible feeling.
"The game needs them both, the game over here needs Seve. He's still got the charisma and I just hope he gets it back because I think golf would really miss him if he decided to walk away from it."
Norman played with Ballesteros, Europe's Ryder Cup captain this year, in a six-man challenge on Tuesday and the advice session on the driving range took place that afternoon.
"I've spent 20 odd years with Seve and he still has an aura with me," said Norman. "Even in the game on Tuesday, he had it.
"Knowing Seve the way I have for 20 years, this has got to be killing him.
"But it's difficult to walk up to a guy with that much talent and that much of a record and give him advice because Seve is a self-made individual. So it's difficult to take the advice.
"It was the same thing with Tom Watson and his putting. Everyone wanted to give Tom advice because we could all see what he was doing wrong."
Norman, the winner of two major titles against five for the Spaniard, invited Ballesteros to try his remedy.
"With myself I had to have a long talk to myself in a mirror to find out what I wanted to get out of myself. You just ask yourself a lot of questions.
"You've got to look yourself dead in the eye. You can't lie to yourself. It's impossible to lie because you know inside what is right and what is wrong for you."

Norman backed Ballesteros over his wish to be a playing captain in the Ryder Cup against the Americans this year if his form improved. "Seve's an inspiration to be around. Absolutely, Seve could be a playing captain without a problem."
